# Plan: Multi-tenant Auth Refactor (reviewed)

Reviewed by /plan-eng-review on 2026-09-10 against PLAN.md at commit 7007835.
Scope was reduced (D4). Six findings, all folded into this plan with the complete remedy.

## Context

**Problem (inferred, author must confirm — see Prerequisite P0 below).** The current auth path
validates tokens with 5 sequential IDP calls, swallows three classes of error inside
`validateAndDispatch()`, and mixes tenant-scoped session logic into a single `legacyAuthFlow()`.
The refactor introduces two focused services, `AuthBroker` (mints and stores tokens) and
`SessionMint` (establishes sessions from cached or freshly minted tokens), on top of the
existing tenant-keyed cache adapter.

**Goal (draft).** Every tenant's login and token validation runs through one explicit,
observable path with bounded latency and no silent failures, while the two invariants below
hold at all times.

**Invariants (draft, must be asserted by tests).**
1. No cross-tenant reads: a token stored under tenant A's key is never returned for tenant B.
2. No resurrection: once a token is invalidated (logout, revocation, tenant suspension, policy
   version bump), no in-flight write can put it back.

**Latency target (draft).** Token validation p95 bounded by the slowest single IDP call plus
cache lookup, not by the sum of five calls. Author to fill in the number.

### Prerequisite P0 (decision D7 → 3A)
Implementation does not start until the author confirms or edits the Problem, Goal,
Invariants and Latency target above. Estimated: human ~30 min / CC ~5 min.

## Existing contracts retained (unchanged from PLAN.md)

The existing cache adapter keys entries by tenant ID, issuer, audience, and policy version.
It evicts expired tokens and invalidates entries on logout, token revocation, or tenant
suspension. It does not serialize mutations. The adapter, its invalidation hooks, and their
existing tests remain in use unchanged. The new services receive the adapter by constructor
injection; nothing new wraps it.

## Architecture (as reviewed)

### Scope (decision D4 → A)
PLAN.md proposed 12 files and five new types (`AuthBroker`, `SessionMint`, `TokenStore`,
`AuthCache`, `RequestPolicy`). Reduced to **two new types**:

| Proposed type | Outcome | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `AuthBroker` | **Keep** | The only writer to the cache; mints tokens via the IDP. |
| `SessionMint` | **Keep** | Reads the cache; asks `AuthBroker` to mint on miss. |
| `AuthCache` | **Drop** | PLAN.md:11-13 describes a pass-through facade over the existing adapter with one backing cache. The adapter is injected directly instead. |
| `TokenStore` | **Drop** | Overlaps the adapter's token storage role. |
| `RequestPolicy` | **Defer** | No consumer named anywhere in the plan. Captured as TODO 1. |

Estimated diff: ~7 files.

### Component and data flow

```
                    per-tenant flag (D6)
   request ──────────┬─────────────────────────────┐
                     │ flag OFF                    │ flag ON
                     ▼                             ▼
             legacyAuthFlow()              validateAndDispatch()  (typed pipeline, D8)
             (unchanged, kept              ├─ parse token        → Result
              until TODO 2)                ├─ verify signature   → Result   (JWKS cache, D10)
                     │                     ├─ check tenant policy→ Result
                     │                     └─ dispatch           → Result
                     │                                │
                     │                                ▼
                     │                     ┌──── error boundary ────┐
                     │                     │ maps each error class  │
                     │                     │ → outcome + log + metric│
                     │                     └────────────────────────┘
                     │                                │
                     ▼                                ▼
               existing adapter  ◄──read──  SessionMint ──mint?──► AuthBroker ──write(gen)──► existing adapter
               (tenant-keyed,                                          │                      (same instance,
                invalidation hooks)                                    ▼                       injected)
                                                          IDP calls (parallel, shared AbortSignal,
                                                          per-call timeout; discovery + JWKS cached)
```

### Issue 1 — Shared cache mutated by two services with no ordering (decision D5 → 1A)
`[P1] (confidence: 8/10) PLAN.md:19-20, PLAN.md:10` — "Both services mutate it" and "they do
not serialize mutations." Failure scenario: `SessionMint` begins minting for tenant A; tenant A
is suspended and the existing hook invalidates A's entries; the in-flight write lands and
restores a valid token. Suspended tenant keeps access silently until expiry.

**Remedy (approved):**
- `AuthBroker` is the **single writer**. `SessionMint` only reads and calls
  `AuthBroker.mint()` on a miss.
- Every write carries the **invalidation generation** it observed at read time. The adapter
  wrapper call in `AuthBroker` compares the generation; a stale write is dropped and logged
  with tenant ID and reason.
- The generation counter is bumped by the existing invalidation hooks (logout, revocation,
  suspension, policy bump). This is one small guard where all writes route through, not a
  guard in every caller.
- Test: deterministic interleaving test (read → invalidate → write) proves the write is dropped.

### Issue 2 — In-place rewrite of legacyAuthFlow() with no rollback (decision D6 → 2A)
`[P1] (confidence: 9/10) PLAN.md:27-28` — "legacyAuthFlow() will get rewritten."

**Remedy (approved):** strangler-fig rollout.
- Keep `legacyAuthFlow()` callable. A **per-tenant flag** routes each tenant to the legacy or
  the `AuthBroker` path.
- Add a counter of requests served by the legacy path (feeds TODO 2's deletion trigger).
- Migrate tenants in waves. Rollback for one tenant is a flag flip, not a revert.
- Deletion of the legacy path and the flag is TODO 2, a separate follow-up.

### Issue 3 — No stated goal or invariants (decision D7 → 3A)
`[P1] (confidence: 9/10) PLAN.md:4-36` — every section describes a smell; none states what
done means. Remedy: the Context section above, confirmed by the author before implementation
(Prerequisite P0).

### Inline ASCII diagrams to add in code
- `AuthBroker`: the read-generation → mint → write-if-current sequence, with the invalidation
  hook bumping the generation drawn alongside.
- `validateAndDispatch()`: the four-step pipeline and the error-boundary mapping table.
- The flag router: legacy vs new path decision.
- Interleaving test file: a timeline comment showing which step of which actor runs when.
Diagram maintenance is part of every later change to these files.

## Code quality (as reviewed)

### Issue 4 — validateAndDispatch() swallows three error classes (decision D8 → 4A)
`[P1] (confidence: 9/10) PLAN.md:23-24` — "three nested try/catch blocks; each catch swallows
a different error class."

**Remedy (approved):**
- Flatten into a straight-line pipeline of small steps (parse, verify signature, check tenant
  policy, dispatch). Each step returns a typed `Result` (reuse ladder: check the repo for an
  existing Result/Either helper first, then an installed dependency, before adding one).
- **One error boundary** maps each error class to a distinct outcome, log line and metric.
  Unknown errors fail closed (reject), never pass.
- Each step gets its own unit test; the boundary gets one table-driven test per error class.
- DRY: cache write logic exists in exactly one place (`AuthBroker`, Issue 1). `SessionMint`
  never duplicates it.

## Tests (as reviewed)

### CRITICAL — Regression: legacyAuthFlow() characterization tests (mandatory, no decision needed)
PLAN.md:27-28 rewrites existing behavior; PLAN.md:15-16 explicitly excludes it from coverage.
Under the regression rule this is a critical requirement:
- **Before** any rewrite, write characterization tests for `legacyAuthFlow()` covering: valid
  token, expired token, revoked token, wrong-tenant token, IDP unavailable, logout then replay,
  tenant suspended then request.
- Run the same fixtures against the `AuthBroker` path under the flag (D6) and assert parity
  where behavior must match, and assert the intended difference where it must not.
- These tests stay until TODO 2 deletes the legacy path, then become new-path-only tests.

### Coverage map (decision D9 → 5A: full map)

```
CODE PATHS                                                USER FLOWS
[~] legacyAuthFlow() (kept behind flag)                   [+] Tenant login via new path
  └── [CRITICAL] characterization: valid / expired          ├── [→E2E] login → mint → validated request
      / revoked / wrong-tenant / IDP down / logout replay    ├── [→E2E] tenant suspended mid-session → rejected
[+] AuthBroker (single writer, versioned write)             └──        flag OFF → legacy path, parity
  ├── write with current generation → stored               [+] Error states (user-visible)
  ├── write with stale generation → dropped + logged         ├── IDP timeout → explicit, retryable error
  ├── mint failure (IDP error) → typed error, no write       ├── malformed token → explicit reject
  └── tenant A key never readable via tenant B key           └── policy miss → explicit reject, never pass
[+] SessionMint (reads, requests mint)
  ├── cache hit → no IDP call
  ├── cache miss → broker mint → stored
  ├── invalidation during mint → no resurrection (interleaving test)
  └── two concurrent mints, same tenant/user → one entry, no corruption
[+] validateAndDispatch() pipeline
  ├── each step happy path
  ├── each error class → distinct outcome + log (table test)
  └── unknown error → fail closed
[+] IDP validation (parallel)
  ├── all calls succeed
  ├── one rejects → others cancelled (assert abort), typed error
  ├── one hangs → per-call timeout fires
  ├── discovery/JWKS served from cache within TTL
  └── unknown kid → JWKS refresh → success (key rotation)
[+] Flag router
  ├── flag ON → new path
  └── flag OFF → legacy path; legacy counter increments

COVERAGE TODAY: 0/23 paths tested (0%)  |  GAPS: 23 (1 CRITICAL regression, 2 E2E)
TARGET AT MERGE: 23/23
```
Legend: [→E2E] needs integration test. No LLM paths, no evals.

### Test requirements (write alongside the code, not after)
| # | Test | Kind | Asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `legacyAuthFlow` characterization | unit + integration | Existing behavior for 7 fixtures listed above (CRITICAL) |
| 2 | `AuthBroker` write current generation | unit | Entry stored under full tenant key |
| 3 | `AuthBroker` write stale generation | unit | Write dropped; log emitted with tenant and reason |
| 4 | `AuthBroker` mint failure | unit | Typed error returned; adapter untouched |
| 5 | Cross-tenant isolation | unit | Store under tenant A; read as tenant B returns miss |
| 6 | `SessionMint` hit / miss | unit | Hit makes zero IDP calls; miss calls broker once |
| 7 | Invalidation during mint | unit (controlled async) | read → invalidate → write; final state is empty |
| 8 | Concurrent mints | unit | One stored entry; both callers get a valid result or a clean error |
| 9 | Pipeline steps | unit | Each step's Result on valid and invalid input |
| 10 | Error boundary | table-driven unit | Each error class → its outcome, log, metric; unknown → reject |
| 11 | IDP all succeed | unit (stubbed IDP) | Result assembled; call count = expected |
| 12 | IDP one rejects | unit | Other calls' AbortSignal aborted; typed error |
| 13 | IDP one hangs | unit (fake timers) | Timeout error within the bound |
| 14 | Discovery/JWKS cache | unit | Second validation makes no discovery/JWKS call |
| 15 | Unknown kid rotation | unit | Refresh once, then verify succeeds |
| 16 | Flag routing | unit | ON → new path; OFF → legacy path + counter |
| 17 | Login → validated request | E2E | Full flow succeeds; second request is a cache hit |
| 18 | Suspend mid-session | E2E | Next request rejected; no token resurrection |

Test framework: none detected in this fixture repo (no `package.json`, zero test files). Match
the real repo's existing convention (`*.test.ts` or `*.spec.ts`) when implementing.

## Performance (as reviewed)

### Issue 6 — Bare Promise.all over 5 IDP calls (decision D10 → 6A)
`[P2] (confidence: 7/10) PLAN.md:31-32` — "parallelized via Promise.all trivially."
Promise.all is fail-fast but does not cancel: the first rejection leaves four calls running
against an already-degraded IDP. 1→5 concurrent calls per request multiplies burst against
rate-limited per-tenant IDPs.

**Remedy (approved):**
- Run the independent calls with `Promise.all`, all sharing one `AbortController` signal;
  the first rejection aborts the rest.
- Each call gets `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` combined with the shared signal, so a hung IDP
  bounds the tail.
- **Cache the discovery document (TTL hours) and JWKS (TTL minutes)** per issuer; on an
  unknown `kid`, refresh once and retry the verification. Hot path drops to 3 or fewer network
  calls. **[Layer 1]** — standard OIDC practice, no new dependency needed.
- Memory: the discovery/JWKS cache is bounded by issuer count, not request count.

No N+1 or database access patterns in scope.

## What already exists
| Existing piece | Plan's use | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Tenant-keyed cache adapter with eviction and invalidation hooks + tests | Reused unchanged, injected | Correct reuse |
| `legacyAuthFlow()` | Was to be rewritten in place | Now kept behind a flag with characterization tests until TODO 2 |
| Module cache singleton semantics | Was relied on via module-level export | Replaced by constructor injection; the global bought nothing |
| `AuthCache` facade (proposed) | Wrapped the adapter | Dropped as duplicate |

## NOT in scope
- `RequestPolicy` — no consumer named; deferred to TODO 1.
- `TokenStore` and `AuthCache` — dropped; the adapter already does this job.
- Changing the adapter's key schema or serializing mutations inside the adapter — the
  generation check in `AuthBroker` closes the race without touching the adapter contract.
- Deleting `legacyAuthFlow()` and the flag — TODO 2, after all tenants migrate.
- Module-wide audit of swallow-and-continue catch blocks — TODO 3, separate diff.
- IDP-side changes, multi-region cache, new artifacts or distribution — none introduced.

## Failure modes
| New codepath | Realistic failure | Test | Handling | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AuthBroker` write | Stale write after invalidation | #7 | Generation check drops + logs | Rejected on next request, log for on-call |
| `AuthBroker` mint | IDP 5xx | #4, #12 | Typed error via boundary | Clear retryable error |
| `SessionMint` read | Wrong tenant key | #5 | Adapter key includes tenant ID | Miss, then mint for own tenant |
| Pipeline boundary | Unmapped error class | #10 | Fail closed | Explicit reject |
| IDP parallel | One call hangs | #13 | Per-call timeout | Timeout error, no spinner |
| JWKS cache | Key rotation | #15 | Refresh on unknown kid | Transparent |
| Flag router | Flag store unavailable | #16 (add case) | Default to legacy path, log | No change in behavior |
| Legacy path | Behavior drift during refactor | #1 (CRITICAL) | Parity assertions | None if tests hold |

**Critical gaps: 0.** The stale-write resurrection race would have been a critical gap (no
test, no handling, silent) under the original plan; decision D5 closes it with test #7.
Flag-store unavailability is added to test #16 as a case.

- Lane A: S1 (independent, test-only, must land before any rewrite)
- Lane B: S2 → S6 (sequential, shared broker/mint module)
- Lane C: S3 (independent)

vs validate) and expect a small import-level merge in the module index.

**What:** Introduce a `RequestPolicy` type once a concrete consumer needs per-request policy
decisions beyond the adapter's policy-version key.
**Why:** Dropped from scope because no plan section names a caller; keeps the author's intent.

**Effort:** M **Priority:** P3 **Depends on:** Refactor merged.

**Why:** A strangler without scheduled demolition is two auth code paths forever.

D5 — Issue 1: AuthBroker and SessionMint both mutate one shared cache with no ordering guard. Who owns writes?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-b3qdhZ on main, PLAN.md:19-20 ("share a global mutable AuthCache ... Both services mutate it") and PLAN.md:10 ("they do not serialize mutations").
ELI10: Two services writing the same tenant-keyed cache with nothing ordering them is a race. Realistic failure: SessionMint starts minting a session for tenant A, the tenant gets suspended and the existing hook invalidates A's entries, then SessionMint's in-flight write lands and puts a fresh token back. A suspended tenant keeps working until the token expires, silently. The existing adapter guarantees validity and tenant keys, but PLAN.md:10 says outright that it does not serialize mutations, so nothing today prevents this. Even with constructor injection (D4), two writers still race.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Revoked or suspended tenants can resurrect access with no error and no log line; that is a security incident, not a bug.
Recommendation: A because a single writer plus a version check on write is explicit, testable, and costs one small guard where all writes route through, which matches your explicit-over-clever and root-cause preferences.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10, C=3/10
Net: one guarded write path versus two unguarded writers that only fail under the timing you never see in tests.

options.label: 1A) Single writer + versioned write (recommended)
options.description: ✅ AuthBroker is the only component that writes tokens; SessionMint reads and asks the broker to mint. Writes carry the invalidation generation they read, and a write with a stale generation is dropped and logged (human: ~1 day / CC: ~20 min). ✅ Testable deterministically: one interleaving test proves a suspended tenant cannot resurrect a token. ❌ Adds a generation counter to the adapter wrapper call path and one more concept to explain.

options.label: 1B) Inject the adapter into both, both still write
options.description: ✅ Removes the module-level global, so tests can pass a fake adapter (human: ~2 hr / CC: ~5 min). ✅ Smallest diff on top of the D4 scope reduction. ❌ The invalidate-then-stale-write race stays; only the failure's discoverability improves.

options.label: 1C) Keep the module-level export as planned
options.description: ✅ Zero additional work beyond what PLAN.md already describes. ✅ Matches the module-cache singleton idiom some TypeScript codebases already use. ❌ Hidden global coupling, untestable without module mocking, and the resurrection race ships unaddressed.

D8 — Issue 4: validateAndDispatch() is 60 lines with three nested try/catch blocks that each swallow an error class. Flatten it?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-b3qdhZ on main, PLAN.md:23-24 ("three nested try/catch blocks; each catch swallows a different error class").
ELI10: A swallowed error means the function keeps going as if nothing happened. In an auth path, that is how an IDP timeout, a malformed token, and a policy lookup miss all turn into the same silent "validation passed" or "validation failed" with no log, no metric and no way for on-call to tell them apart at 3am. The fix is a straight-line pipeline of small steps, each returning a typed result, with one boundary that maps each error class to an explicit outcome and a log line.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Production auth failures stay invisible; the first signal is a customer ticket rather than an alert.
Recommendation: A because a typed pipeline with a single error boundary is explicit over clever, each step gets its own unit test, and the diff is the same size as fixing the swallows in place.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=2/10
Net: three observable, testable failure modes versus three invisible ones.

questions.question:
D10 — Issue 6: 5 sequential IDP calls per validation. Promise.all as planned, or bounded parallelism plus caching?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-b3qdhZ on main, PLAN.md:31-32 ("5 sequential API calls to the IDP; they could be parallelized via Promise.all trivially").
ELI10: Parallelizing is right, but "trivially" hides two problems. Promise.all is fail-fast: when one call rejects, the other four keep running against the IDP with nobody listening, so a flaky IDP now costs 5 wasted calls per failed validation instead of 1. And per-tenant IDPs usually rate-limit; going from 1 to 5 concurrent calls per request multiplies your burst. Separately, at least two of the five calls (discovery document, JWKS signing keys) are static-ish and standard practice is to cache them with a TTL and refresh on unknown key id, which removes those calls entirely rather than speeding them up.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Under IDP degradation the naive version amplifies load on the thing that is already failing, and validation latency stays bound by the slowest of five network calls.
Recommendation: A because AbortController plus a shared signal makes fail-fast actually cancel, per-call timeouts bound the tail, and caching discovery and JWKS is Layer 1 practice that turns 5 calls into 3 or fewer on the hot path.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10, C=3/10
Net: fewer, bounded, cancellable IDP calls versus five unbounded calls that pile onto a degraded IDP.

options.label: 6A) Cancel-on-fail + timeouts + cache discovery/JWKS (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Promise.all over calls sharing one AbortSignal, per-call AbortSignal.timeout, and a TTL cache for discovery and JWKS with refresh on unknown kid (human: ~1.5 days / CC: ~25 min). ✅ Hot path drops to 3 or fewer network calls; failures are typed and bounded; IDP burst per request is capped. ❌ JWKS caching needs the unknown-kid refresh path and its test, or a key rotation locks tenants out.

options.label: 6B) Promise.all + per-call timeouts only
options.description: ✅ Latency drops from sum-of-5 to max-of-5 with bounded tails (human: ~3 hr / CC: ~8 min). ✅ No new cache surface to reason about. ❌ First rejection still leaves four calls running; still 5 calls per validation and 5x burst against rate-limited IDPs.

options.label: 6C) Bare Promise.all as PLAN.md states
options.description: ✅ One-line change, exactly what the plan proposes. ✅ Immediate latency win on the happy path. ❌ No timeouts, no cancellation, no caching: a hung IDP call hangs validation, and failures amplify IDP load.

## Context

Tenant-auth orchestration lives in `legacyAuthFlow()` and a 60-line `validateAndDispatch()` with three nested, error-swallowing try/catch blocks. The goal is to reorganize that orchestration without changing product behavior: same allow/deny outcomes, same status codes, same cache side effects, same IDP call sequence. The original plan proposed 5 new classes across 12 files and no regression coverage for the flow it rewrites. This review cut the plan to 2 classes plus one pure function across ~8 files, made the shared cache dependency explicit, flattened the error handling, and made the "no behavior change" claim checkable with characterization fixtures recorded before any rewrite.

Evidence base: `PLAN.md` only. The fixture repo holds no source or tests, so every finding below quotes plan lines and is a proposal-level finding; runtime behavior is marked unknown where the plan does not state it.

## Context supplied by the plan author (retained)
The goal is to reorganize existing tenant-auth orchestration without changing
its product behavior. RequestPolicy groups the existing per-request access
decision: given already-fetched claims and tenant/request context, it returns
allow or deny under the existing access policy. AuthBroker.validateAndDispatch()
calls it after validation and before dispatch. It adds no policy, network call,
cache mutation or state. Its separate class boundary remains a proposal to review.

## Existing contracts retained (unchanged)
The existing cache adapter keys entries by tenant ID, issuer, audience,
and policy version. It evicts expired tokens and invalidates entries on
logout, token revocation, or tenant suspension. These validity and tenant-key
rules are unchanged; they do not serialize mutations. The adapter, its
invalidation hooks, and their existing tests remain in use unchanged. There is
one backing cache.

## Reviewed architecture (accepted: D6, D7)

Components:
- `AuthBroker` (class) — owns `validateAndDispatch(req)`. Constructor takes `{ cache, idp, clock, logger }`.
- `SessionMint` (class) — owns session minting. Constructor takes `{ cache, clock, logger }`.
- `decideAccess(claims, ctx): AccessDecision` (pure function module, replaces the proposed `RequestPolicy` class) — no imports of adapter, IDP client or clock. `AccessDecision = { kind: 'allow' } | { kind: 'deny', reason }`.
- Composition root (existing app bootstrap module) — creates the single cache adapter instance once and passes it to both services. No module-level exported cache instance anywhere.
- Dropped from the original plan: `AuthCache` facade (D6: adds no behavior over the adapter), `TokenStore` (D5: never described; adapter already owns token persistence).

Data flow:

```
request ──► AuthBroker.validateAndDispatch(req)
              │  1. fetchClaims(req)       ──► IDP client (5 sequential calls, unchanged this PR)
              │  2. lookupCache(key)       ──► injected cache adapter (tenant, issuer, audience, policyVer)
              │                                 hit / miss / expired→evict, exactly as today
              │  3. decideAccess(claims, ctx)   pure: allow | deny(reason)
              │  4. dispatch(handler) on allow  |  reject with today's status on deny
              │
              └─ single catch: KnownErrorClass ─► today's observable outcome + 1 structured log line
                               unknown error   ─► rethrow (never swallowed)

SessionMint.mint(claims) ──► writes one session entry via the SAME injected adapter
                              (invalidated by existing logout / revocation / tenant-suspension hooks)

Composition root:  const cache = createCacheAdapter(...)   // once
                   new AuthBroker({ cache, idp, clock, logger })
                   new SessionMint({ cache, clock, logger })
```

## Code quality (accepted: D8)

`validateAndDispatch()` becomes a linear pipeline of four named helpers (`fetchClaims`, `lookupCache`, `decideAccess`, `dispatch`) with one `catch`. The catch maps each error class the three nested blocks swallow today to the exact observable outcome it produces today, and emits one structured log/metric per formerly silent path. Unknown errors rethrow. Ordering constraint: the R6 characterization fixtures (below) land first so each error class's current outcome is known before it is mapped. The only intentional difference from today is the additive logging.

D8 — What happens to the three nested, error-swallowing try/catch blocks in validateAndDispatch()?
Project/branch/task: main, PLAN.md Multi-tenant Auth Refactor, Section 2 Code quality (structure per D6, wiring per D7).
ELI10: The function that decides whether a request gets in is 60 lines with three try/catch blocks nested inside each other, and each one catches a different kind of error and quietly moves on. D9 — How do we prove the rewritten auth flow behaves exactly like legacyAuthFlow() does today?
Project/branch/task: main, PLAN.md Multi-tenant Auth Refactor, Section 3 Test review, regression rule (structure D6, wiring D7, error pipeline D8 approved).
ELI10: The whole point of this plan is "same behavior, better organized". Right now it plans tests for the new pieces but nothing that compares the new path to the old one, so the only proof of "same behavior" would be users not complaining. A characterization test records what the old code does for every kind of input (good token, expired, revoked, suspended tenant, identity provider down on call 3, and so on) before anything is touched, then runs the same inputs through the new code and demands identical answers. This question settles what must stay identical, what is allowed to differ, and what the acceptance assertions are. Skipping is not an option under the regression rule; the choice is how deep.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Too shallow and a tenant-suspension or revocation path silently changes and someone stays logged in after being revoked; the full matrix costs an afternoon of fixture recording.
Recommendation: A because the input classes are enumerable from the plan's own contracts (PLAN.md:15-17 lists them), recording fixtures against the old code is mechanical, and this is the only test that makes the plan's central claim checkable (human: ~2 days / CC: ~30 min).

## Step 0: Scope Challenge

Evidence base: `PLAN.md` only. The repo holds no source, so every finding quotes plan lines and is a proposal-level finding, not an observed runtime bug. Web research ran via WebSearch (Aside not installed).

**1. What already exists (per the plan's own text)**
- Cache adapter keyed by tenant/issuer/audience/policy-version, with eviction and invalidation hooks and existing tests (`PLAN.md:15-21`). Plan reuses it. Good.
- Per-request allow/deny decision logic (`PLAN.md:8-10`). Plan regroups it as `RequestPolicy`.
- `legacyAuthFlow()` (`PLAN.md:35`). Plan rewrites it. This is the behavior being reorganized, so it is also the oracle for "no product behavior change".

**2. Minimum change for the stated goal ("reorganize without changing product behavior")**
Two things in the plan are not reorganization: the `Promise.all` parallelization (`PLAN.md:39-40`) changes error semantics and IDP call volume, and `TokenStore` (`PLAN.md:43`) is named once and never described. Both are candidates to cut or defer.

**3. Complexity check: 12 files, 5 new classes.** Over both thresholds (8+ files, 2+ classes). Gate fires below.

**4. Search check** [Layer 1, tried and true]: module-level mutable singletons hide dependencies and break test isolation (Jest re-instantiates module graphs per worker); constructor injection is the boring fix. `Promise.all` is fail-fast and still fires all calls; if any of the 5 IDP calls is required, fail-fast is correct, but it changes which error surfaces first. Sources: [OpenReplay on singletons](https://blog.openreplay.com/singletons-javascript-tool-trap/), [DI in Node/TS](https://thetshaped.dev/p/dependency-injection-in-nodejs-and-typescript-dependency-inversion-part-no-body-teaches-you), [MDN Promise.all](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise/all), [allSettled vs all](https://jsmanifest.com/promise-allsettled-vs-promise-all).

**5. TODOS.md:** absent. **6. Completeness:** the plan takes a shortcut on the one test that proves its own goal (regression on `legacyAuthFlow()`). **7. Distribution:** no new artifact, N/A.

**Scope Challenge findings**

| # | Sev | Conf | Source | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | P1 | 9/10 | `PLAN.md:27-28` "share a global mutable `AuthCache` instance via module-level export. Both services mutate it." | Hidden shared dependency; untestable in isolation; two writers, no ownership | pending (Section 1) |

| S7 | P2 | 8/10 | `PLAN.md:31-32` "three nested try/catch blocks; each catch swallows a different error class" | Described but no remedy proposed; swallowing in auth means silent allow/deny errors | pending (Section 2) |
| S8 | P2 | 9/10 | `PLAN.md:43-44` "12 files ... 5 new classes" | Complexity gate | asking now |

Complexity gate: three questions, one at a time. Feature deferrals first (D4, D5), then structure (D6).
